messages:
olga: Customer (acme-marketing) reports huge unexpected credit usage overnight — ~420k embedding tokens burned on a trial account. They say they only kicked off a small nightly sync. Can we triage?

raj: ugh. any request ids or example logs from their side? do we have a user id/email?

olga: their support ticket included a sample request id: req_6c9b1a2f. They attached a stacktrace from their worker and a timestamp around 2026-10-12T03:12:08Z.

sasha: pulled logs for req_6c9b1a2f — I see repeated calls to /v1/embeddings from the same origin IP across a fleet of workers, ~7 calls in ~30s. Retries look like they were immediate.

mike: immediate retries? our default client has exponential backoff with jitter. did they override it?

olga: they said they use our JS SDK but run it inside a serverless cron job that we suspect misfired.

raj: dropped a quick grep on the worker code they pasted. snippet: ```js
// worker sync
await embeddingClient.create({ model: 'embed-small', input: batch });
// naive retry
for (let i=0;i<3;i++) { if (err) retryImmediately(); }
```

sasha: also see in their headers the Authorization key is the LIVE key, not a staging key: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX`. They thought the job ran in staging.

olga: so two possible causes: (1) job duplicated / time-drift caused overlapping runs, (2) immediate retry loop + live key = massive burn.

mike: checking our ingress traces — there's a surge of requests for that customer around that timeframe. trace ids: `tr_91a2b3`, `tr_91a2b4`, `tr_91a2b5`. Latencies were ~120ms but we returned 5xx for a short window (region GC?).

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-10-12_02:58 rolled out to us-west-2. No rollback.

raj: if they hit a transient 5xx and then their retry loop immediately fires across N workers, that multiplies load. If the cron also started twice due to system time drift (we saw NTP update on that host group), that explains x7 duplication.

emma: I want to see the customer's cron schedule and worker concurrency. olga can you ask for the cron config + whether they use leader election / distributed lock?

olga: asked — they replied: `cron: 0 3 * * *` and they run the sync on 8 replicas in k8s without any leader election. They assumed k8s ensures single job but it's a plain Deployment with a scheduled curl inside.

sasha: ok that's the biggest root cause: job runs concurrently across replicas. Combine that with immediate retry on 5xx and a prod key === big burn.

mike: mitigation steps: 1) pause their nightly job (or change key) 2) issue a provisional credit/refund 3) recommend leader election pattern or use our batch endpoint 4) add SDK safety net to block immediate retries on 5xx 5) suggest switching to a staging key for non-prod jobs.

olga: I paused their cron via support console (contacted their infra lead and they accepted).

billing-bot: Automated provisional credit applied: 400k tokens refunded to account acme-marketing; action_id=cr-refund-186543.

emma: thanks. can we also add a short-term guard in the platform: detect a sudden spike of identical requests (same customer, same payload hash) and rate-limit/log before charging?

raj: short-term: we can add a heuristic in API gateway that if there are > N identical embedding requests within T seconds, hold them for manual review and return 429. I'll open an infra ticket.

mike: long-term SDK change: default retry should include jitter + progressive backoff and a max total retry budget. Also if key is tagged as 'staging' vs 'live' we can warn/console log when used from common non-prod endpoints.

olga: customer also mentioned promo code 'ACME50' didn't apply before the burn. I checked: promo was applied but only to subsequent invoices; trial credits were consumed first. They expected promo to reduce embedding unit price retroactively. Need to explain.

emma: action: billing team to confirm promo semantics and whether we can convert part of refund into a promo top-up to satisfy them (customer is a trial high-touch).

billing-bot: Note: promo codes are non-retroactive by policy. Manual top-up possible via support.

olga: customer ok with manual top-up if we also provide engineering recommendations so it doesn't repeat. they've asked for concrete repro steps so they can test a fix.

sasha: repro plan I sent: 1) deploy a Deployment with 3 replicas running a cron `0 3 * * *` that calls our embeddings endpoint 2) intentionally return 503 from a mock upstream for first call 3) run with SDK retry configured to immediate retry (disable jitter) 4) observe N*retries duplicate requests and token consumption 5) switch to leader-election (redis lock) and verify single-run behavior.

mike: attached a minimal repro script (paste into their cluster):
```
# pseudo helm job
replicas: 3
containers:
  - name: sync
    image: acme-sync:latest
    command: ["/bin/sh","-c","while sleep 86400; do node sync.js; done"]
```
and sync.js uses naive retry above.

raj: created infra ticket INF-2026-458 to add temporary identical-request detection + SDK safety param.

olga: support article draft to send to customer with causes, repro steps, and recommended fixes. Will attach refund confirmation and offer manual top-up.

emma: please include example header check for their teams: how to verify they're not accidentally using a live key in non-prod: ```bash
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami
# our endpoint returns key metadata: env=staging|live
```

olga: customer replied: appreciated, accepted refund and requested the help doc. Closing after I send docs and confirm they put leader election in place. :white_check_mark:

mike: follow-ups: (1) refund finalized? (billing-bot answered provisional) (2) add SDK safe defaults PR target 2w (3) infra rate-limiter heuristic rollout to canary next week.

billing-bot: Refund finalized: 400k tokens credited back. ticket=SUP-9821.

olga: thanks everyone. I'll send the support article + repro to customer and update this thread when they confirm fix. :rocket:
